title: Contracted generic subcurve ideals in an etale smooth or nodal chart
statement: Let $A$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$ be its fraction field [def-weil-field], and let $E$ be either $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $n\geq0$, or $A[u,v]/(uv-a)$ for $a\in A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $C$ be a commutative $E$-algebra such that $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $C_K=C\otimes_AK$, equivalently the localization of $C$ at the images of $A\setminus\{0\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change]. Choose any subset $T$ of the finite set of irreducible components of $\operatorname{Spec}C_K$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $I_K$ be the intersection of the minimal prime ideals corresponding to $T$, and $J_K$ the intersection corresponding to its complement; an empty intersection is the unit ideal. Define $I=\{c\in C:c\otimes1\in I_K\}$ and $J=\{c\in C:c\otimes1\in J_K\}$. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset C$ there is $f\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that the ordered pair $(IC_f,JC_f)$ is $(0,C_f)$ or $(C_f,0)$, or, only in the nodal case with $a=0$, $(uC_f,vC_f)$ or $(vC_f,uC_f)$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Here $u,v$ denote the images of the coordinates. In particular $I$ and $J$ are locally finitely generated radical ideals. No properness, valuation-ring, Noetherian-ring, or smoothness-of-the-selected-subcurve hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent relative ideal calculation for Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), with Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve) as the fibrewise analogue. Normal-domain and etale-component algebra: algebra.tex Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal) and Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up). These sources supply ingredients, not the relative assertion verbatim.

proof.text: First consider the polynomial chart, or the nodal chart with $a\ne0$. For the polynomial chart, induction on $n$ using [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain], starting with $A$, shows that $E$ is a normal domain. For the nodal chart apply the last assertion of [lem-sfb-binomial-laurent-normal-form] to $R=A$ and the given nonzero $a$: it states exactly that $E$ is a normal domain, without a Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 030A (lemma-polynomial-domain-normal); binomial case uses the separately stated Laurent-intersection tool, supported by Tags 030A and 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain).

proof.text: In these normal-domain cases, [lem-trf-etale-normal-domain-finite-factors] gives $C\cong\prod_{i=1}^r B_i$, each $B_i$ a normal domain. Every nonzero $s\in A$ is nonzero in $E$: for a polynomial chart this is coefficientwise, and for a nodal chart it follows from the basis assertion of [lem-sfb-binomial-laurent-normal-form]. The $E$-module $C$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Tensor $0\to E\xrightarrow{s}E$ with $C$ using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]; thus multiplication by $s$ is injective on $C$ and on each product factor. In particular no nonzero $s\in A$ becomes zero in any $B_i$.

source.place: Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), via the cited finite-factor consequence; Tags 00U2 (lemma-etale), (6), and 00HD (lemma-flat).

proof.text: Put $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. Localization commutes with a finite product: use a common denominator, the product of the finitely many denominators, to represent any tuple of fractions. Consequently $C_K=\prod_i S^{-1}B_i$, and every factor is a nonzero domain. Its factor kernels are exactly the minimal primes: a prime contains all but one of the orthogonal factor idempotents, and the zero prime of that domain lies below its remaining prime. Their contractions in $C$ are the original factor kernels, since $B_i\to S^{-1}B_i$ is injective. Thus $I$ and $J$ are the complementary product ideals obtained by forcing respectively the selected and unselected coordinates to zero. For a prime $\mathfrak q$ exactly one factor idempotent $e_i$ is outside $\mathfrak q$ (their sum is $1$ and their pairwise products vanish). Taking $f=e_i$ leaves only $B_i$, so $(IC_f,JC_f)$ is $(0,C_f)$ or $(C_f,0)$. For $C=0$ there are no primes and this assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Agent finite-product and fraction calculation, assembling the Tag 030C consequence of step 2; localization is the one specified in the statement.

proof.text: It remains to treat $a=0$. Put $D=C/uC$ and $F=C/vC$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-quotient-base-change], these are etale algebras over $E/(u)=A[v]$ and $E/(v)=A[u]$, respectively. Those two polynomial rings are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain]. Apply [lem-trf-etale-normal-domain-finite-factors] to obtain finite products $D=\prod_i D_i$ and $F=\prod_j F_j$ of normal domains (either product may be empty). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], multiplication by every nonzero $b\in A[v]$ is injective on $D$ and hence on each $D_i$; likewise every nonzero $b\in A[u]$ acts injectively on each $F_j$. In particular each factor is $A$-torsion-free, the image of $v$ in every $D_i$ is nonzero, and that of $u$ in every $F_j$ is nonzero.

The map $E\to E/(u)\oplus E/(v)$ is injective. Indeed the basis $1,u^i,v^j$ of [lem-sfb-binomial-laurent-normal-form] shows that an element killed by both quotients has every coefficient zero. Tensor this injection over $E$ with the flat module $C$, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. The resulting map is $C\to D\oplus F$, $c\mapsto(c\bmod u,c\bmod v)$: the identifications send $\bar e\otimes c$ to $ec$ modulo the relevant ideal. Thus it is injective, equivalently $uC\cap vC=0$.

source.place: Agent basis calculation for the split model of curves.tex Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family); exactness supplied by algebra.tex Tag 00HD (lemma-flat).

proof.text: Let $P_i=\ker(C\to D_i)$ and $Q_j=\ker(C\to F_j)$. These are prime ideals. Every prime of $C$ contains $u$ or $v$ because $uv=0$, and hence contains some $P_i$ or $Q_j$, by the finite-product argument of step 3 in its quotient. Distinct $P_i$ are incomparable: the factor idempotents in $D$ distinguish their kernels and lift to $C$; the same holds for the $Q_j$. Also $u\in P_i$, $v\notin P_i$, while $v\in Q_j$, $u\notin Q_j$, by step 4. Thus no $P_i$ contains a $Q_j$ or conversely. It follows directly that these are precisely the minimal primes of $C$. Their intersection is zero by step 5 and the two product decompositions. Localizing at $S=A\setminus\{0\}$ preserves each kernel and its contraction, because each domain quotient $D_i,F_j$ is $A$-torsion-free: $sc\in P_i$ implies $c\in P_i$, and similarly for $Q_j$. The same prime argument in $C_K$, with its two quotient products $D_K,F_K$, shows that their extensions are precisely its minimal primes. Thus $T$ selects a subset of this finite list, and $I,J$ are exactly the intersections of the selected and complementary kernels in $C$.

source.place: Agent prime-ideal and fraction argument for the split chart; the domain factors and injectivity used here were established in steps 4--5, not inferred merely from the definition of normality.

proof.text:
Fix $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}C$. If $u
otin\mathfrak q$, put $g=u$, so $D_g=0$. Otherwise $\mathfrak q/uC$ is a prime of $D$ and contains all but one of its factor idempotents. Lift the remaining idempotent to $g\in C$; it is outside $\mathfrak q$ and $D_g$ has only that one domain factor localized. Define $h$ in the same way for $F$: take $h=v$ if $v
otin\mathfrak q$, and otherwise lift its unique factor idempotent outside $\mathfrak q/vC$. Set $f=gh
otin\mathfrak q$. Then $D_f$ and $F_f$ are each either zero or a localization of a single domain. At least one is nonzero: the quotient corresponding to a coordinate in $\mathfrak q$ retains the prime induced by $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Agent explicit idempotent-neighbourhood construction in the two finite products; finite-product decomposition is supplied in step 4.

proof.text: Localization of a finite intersection commutes with the intersection: if $c/f^m$ lies in every localized ideal, choose for each ideal a power of $f$ carrying $c$ into it and take the largest power. The same fraction test shows that kernels localize. Therefore step 5 gives $uC_f\cap vC_f=0$, and step 6 computes $IC_f,JC_f$ by intersecting the surviving selected and complementary kernels. If both $D_f$ and $F_f$ are nonzero, the only surviving kernels are $uC_f$ and $vC_f$. If $T$ selects both, their intersection is zero and the complementary empty intersection is $C_f$; if it selects neither the pair is reversed. If it selects only the $D_f$ kernel the pair is $(uC_f,vC_f)$; if only the $F_f$ kernel it is $(vC_f,uC_f)$.

source.place: Agent finite-denominator calculation; compare algebra.tex Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact). No Noetherianity or finite generation of the original contracted ideals is used to shrink.

proof.text: If $D_f=0$, then $uC_f=C_f$ and $F_f=C_f$, by the injection $C_f\to D_f\oplus F_f$ and surjectivity to $F_f$. The latter ring is a nonzero domain, so its sole surviving minimal-prime kernel is zero; selecting it or not gives $(0,C_f)$ or $(C_f,0)$. The case $F_f=0$ is identical with $u,v$ exchanged. This completes the asserted list in the $a=0$ case. Finally $I,J$ are radical globally: if $c^m$ belongs to a contracted intersection of prime ideals of $C_K$, primality puts $c\otimes1$ in every one of them. On each constructed $D(f)$ the ideals are zero, the unit ideal, or generated by the single coordinate $u$ or $v$. They are therefore locally finitely generated. Empty $T$ and full $T$ use the stipulated unit empty intersection, and all arguments include the zero algebra.
